body: Couldn't `ScriptEditor` inherit from `DocumentEditorContainer`? This would remove the need for re-declaring all of the public functions from `DocumentEditorContainer`
ScriptEditor is exposed, so it can't inherit from a non-exposed class.
These would fit better in `ScriptEditor`
I think the name doesn't quite fit since it also returns `EditorHelp` which isn't a editor. Maybe just `get_all_tabs`
These can be moved to the other `ScriptEditor` definitions

`edited_scene_changed`, `apply_scripts`, `ensure_select_current`, `get_unsaved_scripts`, `set_window_layout`, and `get_window_layout` are only used by `ScriptEditorPlugin` it could call them directly through `get_script_container`. I think having functions for these bloats `ScriptEditor` unnecessarily. There are also functions which are only called once or twice from other classes like `save_current_script` and `open_text_file_create_dialog`

`get_active_editor` and `get_resource_editor` are not used

`open_find_in_files_dialog` was removed

I agree, lots of methods can actually be moved out but I wanted to keep this PR straightforward. I'm planning a followup to move more of them in addition to the ones moved out in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122143

The full name would be `get_all_document_editors`, the whole `DocumentEditorContainer` name is because all the controls in it are what I'm calling `DocumentEditors`, which includes editor help. It's not really an editor but its the best name I have for all of them collectively. I see it as a 'read-only' documentation editor or something. And I'm planning to make `EditorHelp` inherit `ScriptEditorBase` in the future too.

Makes sense, thanks for checking these. 
I didn't change the ones used in external files since I didn't want more files changed and some may be moved in a followup anyway.

It'd be better to keep methods in their original place, trying to sync the positions only makes noisy diff. Rearranging can be done in a separate PR.

EDIT:
Actually nevermind, the changes are simple enough.
This might need switching to `force_focus_dock()` now, because you can't jump to debugger errors while in Game view etc.

Since you are changing it...
```suggestion
	void set_scene_root_script(const Ref<Script> &p_script);
```
The `p_script.is_valid()` can be checked at the beginning and do an early return.
Since all this does is call `reload_open_files()`, you can just connect to `script_container)` directly.
Somewhat unrelated, but this initialization should be done in the header.
- Fixed in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123564
Since the script editor can move in tree now, this should probably use `NOTIFICATION_READY`. `NOTIFICATION_POSTINITIALIZE` should work too I think.

If you are doing it this way, the extra variable is redundant.

```suggestion
	if (should_use_external_editor(p_script)) {
```

You could also merge it into the previous condition (i.e. scirpt is null || use external).
Same in DocumentEditorContainer btw.

Some methods that are called after `_apply_editor_settings()` rely on editor settings though, and I would need to go through to make sure each of them would be fine with moving to ready or if they are needed on enter tree. It's getting out of scope for what this PR is for too, I think it can be done later.
